  A. RESOLUTION NO. 22-11 REAUTHORIZING THE CITY COUNCIL AND THE

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-11 regarding

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 1, 2022  2
   1. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of January 18, 2022.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of January 25, 2022.

  Recommended Action: Approval.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  D. MONTHLY BUDGET UPDATE – DECEMBER 2021

  This report provides the monthly budget update for the City’s General Fund
  and Mission Playhouse as of December 31, 2021 (prior to the monthly closing
  entries). The monthly budget update incorporates the actual revenue received
  and expenditures that have occurred through December 31, 2021, and projects
  the financial results for the year ending on June 30, 2022.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the report.

  E. ADOPTION AND SECOND READING OF ORDINANCE NO. 683: AMENDING
  CHAPTER 153 OF THE SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE TO ADDRESS THE
  NEW STATE LAW (SENATE BILL 9) THAT WOULD ALLOW SINGLE-FAMILY-
  ZONED PROPERTIES TO BE SUBDIVIDED INTO TWO LOTS AND THE
  DEVELOPMENT OF TWO URBAN DWELLING UNITS (ZTA21-003)

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 683 would amend Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning
  Code) in order to amend the zoning definitions and development standards to
  allow for the development of urban lot splits and urban dwelling units on
  single-family-zoned properties, consistent with the applicable State law.
  Introduction and first reading of Ordinance No. 683 was conducted with a 4-0
  vote of the City Council on January 18, 2022 City Council meeting. If adopted,
  the Ordinance would become effective 30 days after adoption.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 1, 2022  3
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council conduct second reading by title only
  and adopt Ordinance No. 683 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the
  City of San Gabriel, California, Approving Planning Case No. ZTA21-003,
  Amending Title XV, Chapter 153 (Zoning) that would allow single-family-zoned
  properties to be subdivided into two lots and allow for the development of two
  urban dwelling units”.

  F. EXTENSION OF EXCLUSIVE NEGOTIATION AGREEMENT WITH RELATED
  COMPANIES OF CALIFORNIA, LLC

  For the past year and a half, City staff, Related Companies representatives and
  staff from the San Gabriel Valley Council of Governments (“Authority”) have
  been negotiating for the acquisition of 405 South Del Mar Avenue, owned by
  the Authority for the purpose of Related Companies constructing an affordable
  housing project on the site. Related and the City have an Exclusive Negotiation
  Agreement in place. Due to reasons set out in the staff report, the Agreement
  needs to be extended by City Council’s action.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Amendment to the
  Exclusive Negotiation Agreement and authorize the City Manager to execute it.

  G. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 73968 FOR 306 SAN MARCOS
  STREET PLANNING CASE NO. PL-15-045

  The development, located at 306 San Marcos Street, is an 8-unit condominium
  project. The Final Tract Map is for a single lot that will be subdivided into the
  condominium airspaces for the development. Staff and the Los Angeles County
  Department of Public Works have reviewed the Final Tract Map and have
  determined it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, conditions
  of approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Authorize the City Manager to execute the Subdivision Improvement
  Agreement; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 1, 2022  4
   2. Authorize the City Manager to accept Final Tract Map No. 73968 and
  authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County
  Clerk’s office.

  H. ACCEPTANCE OF FINAL TRACT MAP NO. 73648 FOR 328 EAST LIVE OAK
  STREET PLANNING CASE NO. PL-15-073

  The development, located at 328 East Live Oak Street, is a 10-unit condominium
  project. The Final Tract Map is for a single lot that will be subdivided into the
  condominium airspaces for the development. Staff and the Los Angeles County
  Department of Public Works have reviewed the Final Tract Map and have
  determined it is in compliance with the State Subdivision Map Act, conditions
  of approval, and the City’s ordinances regarding subdivisions.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council accept Final Tract Map No. 73648 and
  authorize filing with the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk’s
  office.

  I. INSTRUCTIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is requesting authorization to enter into an
  agreement with East Los Angeles College (ELAC) for an Instructional Services
  Agreement (ISA) for members of the Fire Department. ISA were set up by the
  State Chancellor’s Office to provide college level credit for specific training that
  was mandated for public agencies each year. There is no cost on part of the
  City. The Fire Department will receive a lump sum payment once a year based
  on the recorded number of hours toward training of advanced personnel.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Instructional Services
  Agreement and authorize the Fire Chief to enter into the agreement with ELAC
  on behalf of the San Gabriel Fire Department and create an account to deposit
  ISA funds for the purpose of purchasing equipment or procuring training from
  a provider as needed.

  J. CALIFORNIA JOINT APPRENTICESHIP COMMITTEE (Cal-JAC)

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is requesting authorization to enter into a
  subscription agreement with the Cal-JAC to develop an apprenticeship
  program for new recruits and newly-promoted members. The California

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 1, 2022  5
   Firefighter Joint Apprenticeship Committee is responsible  for  the
  administration of the Standards for the Cal-JAC Program.

  Recommended Action:
  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the subscription agreement
  with Cal-JAC and authorize the Fire Chief to enter into the agreement with Cal-
  JAC on behalf of the San Gabriel Fire Department and create an account to
  deposit Cal-JAC funds for the purpose of purchasing equipment or providing
  training.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE FOR THE SIXTH CYCLE (2021-2029)

  The California Government Code Section 65302(c) requires cities and counties
  to include a housing element in its general plan, and that the housing element
  must be updated periodically to reflect current conditions and legal
  requirements. The City’s current Housing Element was adopted in 2013 for the
  planning period between 2013-2021 (5th Cycle). State law requires that the
  Housing Element be updated for the 2021-2029 planning period (6th Cycle).

  The Housing Element is required to identify and analyze existing and projected
  housing needs, and include statements of the City’s goals, policies, quantified
  objectives, and programs for the preservation, improvement, and development
  of housing for all income levels, particularly the provision of housing affordable
  to low- and moderate-income households. In adopting its Housing Element
  Update, the City must consider local conditions and contest, including
  economic, environmental, and fiscal factors, a s well as community goals as set
  forth in the General Plan.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss the proposed Resolution;

  2. Adopt Resolution No. 22-10 of the City Council of San Gabriel, California
  approving the proposed Initial Study/Negative Declaration and 2021-2029
  Housing Element Update; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to make technical changes and
  other, non-substantive, edits to the 2021-2029 Housing Element that may result
  from the Department of Housing and Community Development review for final

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 1, 2022  6
   certification of the Housing Element, without further City Council consideration
  or re-adoption of the 2021-2029 Housing Element.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.
 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. ANALYSIS OF REFINANCING OPTIONS FOR THE CITIZENS BUSINESS BANK
  LOAN

  In December of 2014, the City borrowed $7.8 million from Citizens Business
  Bank (CBB) for the construction of the Public Works maintenance facility. The
  City was required to provide collateral for the loan in the form of a 10-year
  certificate of deposit for the loan amount. The General Fund cash used as
  collateral for the loan is restricted. City staff has solicited and received offers to
  refinance the loan. The City has also asked its financial advisor, Urban Futures,
  Incorporated, to analyze the City’s loan options, solicit additional offers, and
  provide an analysis of the City’s refinancing options.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council direct staff to maintain the current
  terms of the CBB loan agreement and continue to monitor opportunities to
  refinance the loan as the City’s financial condition improves.

  B. DECLARATION OF VACANCY OF COUNCIL MEMBER OFFICE AND
  CONSIDERATION OF PROCESS TO FILL VACANCY

  The resignation of Mayor Liao on January 27, 2022, creates the need for the
  City Council to take action to fill the vacant seat. The Council will consider the
  options allowed for this process, pursuant to Government Code Section
  36512(b).

  Recommended Action:

  Due to the cost involved with holding an election and the delay in seating a
  replacement councilmember, staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Accept resignation of Mayor Liao, with regrets, effective January 27, 2022.
  2. Adopt Resolution No. 22-09, adopting a process for filling of vacancy on the
  City Council by appointment.

  C. CITY COUNCIL SELECTION OF VICE MAYOR

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – February 1, 2022  7
   The City Council will select a new vice mayor to serve until the City Council
  reorganizes in March 2022.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT
  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
